title: Mock 5 · Mixed Revision
blurb: A full-syllabus sweep weighted like the real exam, mixing 2026 updates with the classic basics.

questions.q: Deciding whether to manage your own investments or outsource them to a mutual fund should be broken down into which three questions?
options: Can I do it? Do I want to do it? Can I afford to outsource?
Is it safe? Is it liquid? Is it tax-free?
What is the NAV? What is the load? What is the TER?
Who is the sponsor? Who is the trustee? Who is the custodian?
questions.explanation: The workbook frames the choice as ability (can one do it), willingness (does one want to) and affordability (can one afford to outsource).

questions.q: From its 1979 base of 100, the Sensex reached about 82,269 by 30 January 2026. Roughly what annual compounded appreciation does this represent (before dividends)?
questions.explanation: The workbook states this is an appreciation of around 15.4% p.a., compounded annually, before adding dividends.

questions.q: What is the minimum investment amount for a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF)?
options: ₹10 lakh across all investment strategies of the same AMC
questions.explanation: SEBI's SIF product line requires a minimum of ₹10 lakh from the investor across all investment strategies of the same AMC.

questions.q: A Fund of Funds must invest at least what share of its total assets in the underlying fund?
questions.explanation: FoFs (overseas or domestic) must invest at least 95% in the underlying fund, the same threshold as index funds/ETFs for index constituents.

questions.q: A Credit Risk Fund must invest at least 65% of its assets in corporate bonds rated:
questions.explanation: Credit risk funds invest at least 65% in AA and below-rated corporate bonds (AA+ excluded). Corporate bond funds invest 80% in AA+ and above.
hints: That is the corporate bond fund rule.

questions.q: Under the SEBI MF Regulations 2026, the Unit Holder Protection Committee (UHPC) is constituted by, and reports to the board of:
questions.explanation: The AMC must constitute a UHPC, which submits its report and recommendations to the AMC's board of directors and monitors their implementation.

questions.q: The two depositories in India that can hold mutual fund units in dematerialised form are:
questions.explanation: India's two depositories are National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository Services Limited (CDSL); investors deal with them through depository participants.

questions.q: Which SEBI circular provided for the new cadre of mutual fund distributors?
options: Circular of 1 February 2018 on TRI benchmarking
Circular of 27 October 2021 on two-tier benchmarks
Circular of 13 June 2023 on execution-only platforms
questions.explanation: SEBI circular CIR/IMD/DF/21/2012 dated 13 September 2012 allowed empanelment of a new cadre of distributors selling simple and performing schemes.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the persons considered for the new cadre of distributors?
options: Retired government officials (Class III and above) with 10+ years of service
Serving fund managers of an AMC
questions.explanation: The new cadre comprises postal agents, retired govt/semi-govt officials and retired bank officers with 10+ years of service, and similar persons such as bank correspondents. Serving fund managers are not in the list.

questions.q: The final SID and SAI, after incorporating SEBI's observations, must be hosted on AMFI's website:
options: On the day the issue closes
questions.explanation: Final documents must be on AMFI's website two days before the issue opens. Drafts are available on SEBI's website.

questions.q: How frequently must DEBT schemes disclose their portfolios?
options: Fortnightly, within 5 days of each fortnight
questions.explanation: Debt schemes disclose their portfolio fortnightly within 5 days of every fortnight, along with the yield of instruments, in addition to the monthly disclosure.

questions.q: The principle that an investor who signs the application form is presumed to have read the scheme documents is called:
questions.explanation: Mutual fund investments are governed by caveat emptor ('let the buyer beware'); an investor can't later claim to be unaware of facts disclosed in the documents.
hints: A legal doctrine on decided matters.

questions.q: The additional commission for onboarding an eligible new investor through a lump sum investment is 1% of the first application subject to a maximum of:
questions.explanation: Lump sum: 1% of the first application, capped at ₹2,000, provided the investor stays invested for at least one year. SIP: 1% of the first year's total, also capped at ₹2,000.

questions.q: Under SEBI's PFUTP Regulations, which of these amounts to mis-selling of mutual fund units?
options: Not taking reasonable care to ensure the suitability of the scheme to the buyer
Recommending an index fund to a first-time investor
questions.explanation: Mis-selling includes false or misleading statements, concealing material facts or risk factors, and not taking reasonable care to ensure suitability.

questions.q: Which risk-adjusted return measure is MANDATORY for AMCs to disclose, on a daily basis?
questions.explanation: The Information Ratio is the only risk-adjusted return measure AMCs must disclose, daily on their website and comparably on AMFI's.
hints: Commonly shown in factsheets, but not mandatory.

questions.q: The NAV of a scheme is ₹50 and an exit load of 1% applies. What price does the redeeming investor receive per unit?
questions.explanation: Repurchase price = NAV × (1 − load) = 50 × 0.99 = ₹49.50.
hints: The load is deducted, not added.

questions.q: The risk that interest and maturity proceeds from a bond portfolio can only be reinvested at rates lower than originally assumed is called:
questions.explanation: Reinvestment risk concerns the rate at which interim cash flows (the 'interest on interest' component) can be reinvested.
hints: Relates to government and policy actions.

questions.q: For equity-oriented funds bought before the change, which date's value is used for grandfathering long-term capital gains?
questions.explanation: Gains up to 31 January 2018 are grandfathered; the cost is taken as the higher of the purchase price or the NAV on 31 January 2018.
hints: The LTCG tax started then, but not the grandfathering date.
That is the date the new tax rates apply to redemptions.

questions.q: Unabsorbed capital losses can be carried forward for up to:
questions.explanation: Unabsorbed capital loss can be carried forward up to 8 years.

questions.q: An investor has had no transaction in any of his folios for the six months ending September. How will he receive a Consolidated Account Statement?
questions.explanation: Investors with no transaction in the preceding six months (ending September or March) get a half-yearly CAS; those who transact get a monthly CAS.
hints: Monthly CAS is for months with transactions.

questions.q: A distributor collects a redemption form from a client at 1 pm but submits it at the AMC's Official Point of Acceptance at 4 pm. Which time decides the applicable NAV?
options: The time the RTA processes it next day
4 pm, the time stamped at the OPoA
questions.explanation: Time stamping is done at the official point of acceptance; the time of submission there, not when the distributor received it, is what counts for cut-off.
hints: The distributor is not an OPoA.

questions.q: The SIP Pause facility allows an investor to temporarily stop SIP instalments, typically for:
options: 1 to 6 months, without cancelling the mandate
questions.explanation: SIP pause halts deductions for 1 to 6 months (depending on the AMC); the SIP resumes automatically and the mandate is retained.
hints: Pause is temporary and keeps the mandate.

questions.q: What happens to the existing SIP in a minor's folio once the minor attains majority?
options: It continues automatically under the guardian
It ceases to be executed from the date of majority until the status is changed and a fresh mandate is given
It is converted into an SWP
questions.explanation: SIPs, SWPs and STPs in a minor's folio run only till the date of majority. The folio is frozen until the change of status (MAM form, PAN, KYC, bank details) and a fresh mandate is registered.
hints: The guardian can't operate after majority.

questions.q: What share of unitholders can terminate the appointment of an AMC or pass a resolution to wind up a scheme?
questions.explanation: 75% of unitholders (unitholding) can terminate the AMC's appointment or resolve to wind up a scheme.

questions.q: Under AMFI's code, how must a mutual fund distributor display the tagline 'AMFI-registered Mutual Fund Distributor' in printed communication?
options: In a clear, legible font of at least size 12, with or below their name
Only in the investor's vernacular language
questions.explanation: MFDs must display the tagline along with or below their name in at least font size 12 in all printed communication, and clearly in all other communication.
hints: Required in all forms of communication.
